original_question: Which region of chromosome 5 contains the mutated gene associated with hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis?

final_qi.question: Which region of chromosome 5 contains the mutated gene associated with hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis?
final_qi.long_answer: The hereditary (autosomal-recessive) form of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis has been linked to mutations/deletions in the GM-CSF (CSF2) locus, which is situated on the long arm of chromosome 5 at band q31 (5q31). Loss of GM-CSF signalling from this 5q31 region prevents surfactant clearance by alveolar macrophages, producing the characteristic proteinosis.

final_answer.long_answer: Hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis can result from loss-of-function mutations in the CSF2 (granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor) gene. CSF2 lies in the cytokine gene cluster on the long arm of chromosome 5, band q31. Mutation of this 5q31 locus disrupts GM-CSF signalling to alveolar macrophages, preventing surfactant clearance and producing the proteinosis phenotype.
